newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK leader-designate moves to form post-1997 team.
newsitem.headline: HK leader-designate moves to form post-1997 team.

text.p: Hong Kong's leader-designate Tung Chee-hwa moved closer to forming his post-colonial administration on Saturday with the recruitment of the territory's popular top civil servant Anson Chan.
Tung, who spoke with Chief Secretary Chan over breakfast, also told reporters he would meet all principal officials of the existing government starting from Monday.
"I have asked Mrs Chan to stay on to work for the future Hong Kong government. I'm very happy that she has agreed to accept," Tung told reporters after their 105-minute meeting.

"She would also arrange for me to meet the 24 policy secretaries next week," Tung said after his first meeting with Chan since he was chosen on December 11 by a China-controlled committee to head Hong Kong from next July 1 after Britain's withdrawal.
Tung also pledged to respect the political neutrality of the territory's civil service.
"Whether it's her or the 180,000 civil servants, maintaining political neutrality is very important...I will definitely respect that," shipping magnate Tung said.
Chan, 56, appearing relaxed and smiling next to Tung outside his luxury seaside villa on Hong Kong island, thanked Tung for asking her to stay on in her job.
"I'm extremely grateful to Mr Tung for requesting me to stay on and for his trust in me. I'm of course delighted to accept," Chan told reporters.
She also said she had called on Tung to allow all principal officials to stay on after the handover to assure continuity of government after the resumption of Chinese control.
"I very much hope that on the conclusion of these meetings with individual policy secretaries that Mr Tung will be able to make up his mind about his team," she said.

"I personally feel that if it is possible for all the principal officials to straddle 1997 and continue to serve the people of Hong Kong, this would do a great deal to instil confidence and maintain morale in the civil service," she said.

With only 185 days left until the handover, Tung is moving quickly to assemble a cabinet and to hammer out his relationship with a provisional legislature that China created last week to replace the existing chamber at the sovereignty transfer.

He has called an informal luncheon meeting of the 60 legislature members next Monday, which is expected to discuss the scope of the body's lawmaking activities and possible candidates as speaker of the assembly, although no agenda has yet been set.

Chan, second-in-command to colonial Governor Chris Patten, enjoys a high degree of respect and popularity in the territory and has been people's favourite to run Hong Kong when more than 150 years of British colonial rule ends.
But while she has consistently topped popularity polls, she did not formally enter the contest to become Hong Kong's leader.

Many officials -- in Hong Kong, in Britain and in China -- respect Chan's administrative talent and consider the Tung-Chan ticket as a "dream team" scenario likely to promote Hong Kong's smooth transition to Chinese rule.
Chan also said some government officials would be seconded next week to assist Tung in setting up his private office and that a car and chauffeur have been provided for his personal use.
